name: Bildad
bio: Bildad the Shuhite, one of Job's three friends, traveled with Eliphaz and Zophar to mourn with him and comfort him after disaster struck his family and health, sitting with him in silence for seven days before anyone spoke (Job 2:11-13). His lengthy speeches arguing that Job's suffering must be deserved punishment for sin are told in detail in the chapters ahead. Across three speeches (Job 8, 18, 25), Bildad appealed to the wisdom of earlier generations and the fate of the wicked to argue that Job's suffering proved some hidden guilt, growing shorter each time; his final speech simply insisted that no mortal can be truly righteous or pure before God. Afterward, the LORD rebuked him and Eliphaz for not speaking rightly about God as Job had, and had him offer sacrifices alongside Eliphaz and Zophar while Job prayed for them; the LORD accepted Job's prayer on their behalf (Job 42:7-9).
